Juha Rantanen
Espoo, Finland
juha.rantanen@mail.example | +358 00 000 0123


EDUCATION

MSc Electrical Engineering
CRIT, Cambridge, MA, USA
Graduated 2024


PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Signal Processing Engineer | Tuulenkaari Satellite Systems | January 2025 – present

- Implemented digital beamforming algorithms for a 64-element L-band planar array receiver on Tuulenkaari’s LEO imaging radar satellite programme. Designed the beamforming weight computation pipeline and validated the full receive chain from antenna pattern measurement through to calibrated beam outputs.
- Wrote the C firmware for the onboard digital back-end processor (Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+), implementing range compression, pulse repetition interval scheduling, and real-time housekeeping under hard sub-millisecond timing constraints.
- Built the ground-segment SAR data-processing pipeline in Python: orbit-corrected image formation, geocoding, radiometric calibration. Tested, version-controlled, documented, and used daily by the operations team. Approximately 18 000 lines of production code.
- Performed RF characterisation of the L-band receive chain: noise figure, gain stability across temperature, and antenna pattern verification using Keysight ENA and R&S FSW instruments in the company’s RF lab.
- Designed and tuned an extended Kalman filter for real-time orbit determination from GPS pseudorange measurements, feeding the motion compensation loop in the SAR ground processor.
- All work on a LEO satellite instrument — directly on a spaceborne platform from subsystem design through integration and test.
- Co-authored a paper presented at the Baltic Microwave Conference (BaMC 2025) on digital beamforming calibration techniques for LEO SAR receivers.
- Finnish citizen. EU work authorisation.
- All work at Tuulenkaari conducted in English across a team of twelve engineers from six countries.


PROJECTS

Onboard Self-Calibration Module (Tuulenkaari, 2025)
Led a three-person sub-team delivering the satellite’s antenna-array self-calibration module. Assigned work packages, ran weekly integration reviews, and delivered the module on schedule within a ten-week programme.

Currently based in Espoo. Ready to relocate to Oulu for the right opportunity; the space-systems engineering cluster there is specifically attractive.


SKILLS

- Digital beamforming, SAR image formation, array signal processing
- C/C++, Python, MATLAB, Simulink, Xilinx Vivado
- RF test instrumentation (network analysers, spectrum analysers)
- Linux, git, CI/CD pipelines
- Finnish (native), English (fluent)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
The Senior Signal Processing Engineer position at Kaikuvaara is a close match to what I’ve been doing at Tuulenkaari Satellite Systems, and it’s the direction I want my career to go.

I’ll be specific rather than general. My MSc at CRIT was in Electrical Engineering, and I chose the programme because I wanted to work on systems that fly. My thesis was on space-time adaptive processing for synthetic aperture radar — the part of SAR image formation where you deal with clutter, interference, and platform motion simultaneously. The coursework and thesis gave me a solid foundation in statistical signal processing, electromagnetic theory, and estimation, and they shaped my decision to join Tuulenkaari immediately after graduating.

In the eighteen months since, I’ve been working on Tuulenkaari’s LEO imaging radar programme. What I’ve actually shipped, briefly: a 64-element digital beamforming receiver from algorithm design through hardware validation; the C firmware for the onboard signal processor; a production Python ground-segment pipeline used daily by the ops team; an extended Kalman filter for orbit determination; and RF characterisation of the full receive chain in the lab. I also led a three-person team that delivered the antenna self-calibration module, and co-authored a conference paper on the beamforming calibration approach. All of this on a satellite programme, so the platform experience is directly spaceborne.

I’m listing these not to recite my CV but because the overlap with Kaikuvaara’s work is unusually direct. You build signal-processing electronics for SAR and scatterometer payloads. I have been building a SAR signal-processing chain from the firmware up. The transition would be to a company with more heritage in the space, working on a broader portfolio of instruments, in a city with a stronger ecosystem for exactly this work.

What I’m looking for specifically is that engineering maturity. Tuulenkaari is building its first satellite, and the learning curve has been steep for everyone, including the company. Kaikuvaara has been delivering instruments that fly for years, and that depth of experience is what I want to be learning from at this stage. The environment matters as much as the work itself when you’re early-career, and an established signal-processing group in a city with Suvanto, the university’s research groups, and the rest of the local space cluster is a stronger foundation for long-term growth than a startup’s first programme.

I’m aware that eighteen months is short for a senior title. What I can point to is the scope and intensity of the work, not years of tenure. If the role is open to someone whose experience is compressed but concrete, I believe there is a strong fit.

I can start with reasonable notice and am flexible on timing.

Juha Rantanen

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
